critical_violations.title: Off-Label Promotion
critical_violations.response: Off-label promotion isn't compliant with ABPI rules. Stick to approved indications only.

critical_violations.title: Unqualified Safety Claims
critical_violations.description: Claims like 'no side effects', 'completely safe', 'zero risk'
critical_violations.response: According to ABPI, you can't claim a medicine has no side effects. Mention the actual safety profile with specific data.

critical_violations.title: Unsubstantiated Superlatives
critical_violations.response: Superlative claims like 'best' need robust clinical evidence per ABPI rules. Use specific trial data instead.

critical_violations.title: Gifts or Inducements
critical_violations.description: Offering anything of value to influence prescribing
critical_violations.response: Offering gifts or inducements doesn't comply with ABPI rules. Follow your company's proper sample request process.

critical_violations.title: Competitor Disparagement
critical_violations.description: Negative comments about competitors without data
critical_violations.response: According to ABPI, you shouldn't criticize a competitor outside results of a clinical trial. Be factual and objective.

critical_violations.title: Pre-Marketing Promotion
critical_violations.response: Pre-marketing promotion isn't compliant with ABPI rules. You can only discuss authorized products.

critical_violations.title: Lavish Hospitality
critical_violations.description: Inviting doctors to expensive venues or high-end restaurants
critical_violations.response: Inviting a doctor to a luxury venue doesn't comply with ABPI rules on hospitality. Keep it modest and professional.

coaching_instructions: When you detect these patterns, mention the compliance issue briefly and suggest an alternative. Keep it conversational and helpful, not legalistic. Never mention asterisks or read out the ABPI rule clauses.
